Together we soar...
Welcome
Welcome to Bitterne Church of England Primary School.
Welcome to Bitterne Church of England Primary School, a warm, inclusive two-form entry primary school for children from Year R to Year 6, situated in the heart of Bitterne village in Southampton. We are proud to serve our local community and to welcome families from across the city and beyond.
At Bitterne, we believe that every child matters. We are a community school with a strong Christian foundation, guided by our core values of Hope, Courage and Creativity. These values shape the way we care for our children, support their learning and work together as a school community. Our aim is simple: to give every child the very best start in life in a kind, respectful and nurturing environment.
Our school motto captures what we stand for: Every child, their Own Path… Be Ambitious, Be Kind, Be You.
We make learning fun, engaging and meaningful, starting from day one in Year R, where children build strong foundations through play, exploration and positive relationships. As children grow, they are encouraged to be curious, confident learners who enjoy coming to school and are proud of their achievements.
Every child at Bitterne is known as an individual. We carefully support and challenge pupils to meet their needs, helping them to develop academically while also nurturing their social and emotional wellbeing. Alongside this strong focus on care and wellbeing, we have high expectations for learning and are ambitious for every child’s success.
We believe that children thrive when schools and families work together, and we place great importance on working in close partnership with parents and carers. We are a highly inclusive school, where everyone is welcome and diversity is celebrated.
Above all, Bitterne is a caring community where children feel safe, valued and encouraged to be ambitious and follow their own path.
We very much look forward to welcoming you and your child into our school community and working in close partnership with you throughout their primary years. If you have not yet visited us, we warmly encourage you to do so and see our school in action. We would be delighted to meet you, answer your questions and share more about life at Bitterne.
Mrs Jen Johnson Headteacher
The St. Mary's Partnership
We are proud to be part of the St Mary’s Partnership, a collective of four schools in Southampton dedicated to improving educational outcomes and life chances for children in our city.

Home / School Partnership
Welcome to Our Parent Partnership Page
At our school, we believe that working together ensures the best outcomes for our children. Your partnership is vital, and we are here to support you every step of the way. If you ever have concerns or need guidance, please don’t hesitate to come and talk to us.
Family Support Officer
Mrs. Amy Davies is our dedicated Family Support Officer. She is available to support parents and carers with any concerns you may have. Mrs. Davies is in school from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, ready to listen, guide, and assist in any way she can.
Staying Connected
We use ClassDojo as our primary communication tool. Through ClassDojo, you will receive:
In addition to ClassDojo, we send out a monthly newsletter packed with updates, upcoming events, and useful information.

Daily Opportunities to Connect
Our teachers are available at classroom doors at the end of each school day to answer any quick questions or discuss minor concerns. This is a wonderful opportunity to stay in touch with your child’s teacher and maintain an open line of communication.
Engaging with Your Child’s Education

Home-School Agreement
Our Home-School Agreement outlines the shared responsibilities of parents, carers, staff, and students in creating a supportive and effective learning environment. By working together, we ensure the best outcomes for every child.

PE and Sports Premium
Bitterne CE Primary School is committed to providing a well-rounded education that nurtures the whole child. Physical education, school sport and physical activity (PESSPA) play a vital role in this, supporting the development of our pupils' physical, mental, and social well-being.
PE and Sports Premium Grant
In 2013, the Government introduced the PE and Sport Premium, a funding stream designed to improve the quality and provision of PEESPA in primary schools. The Government stated that:‘ Schools must use the funding to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of PE and sport they offer'. Aligning with Our Values
Our commitment to PE and sport is underpinned by the core values that guide our school: love, trust, and forgiveness. Through physical activity, our pupils learn the importance of teamwork, sportsmanship, and perseverance - values that are essential for their personal growth and development.
Nurturing the Whole Child
At Bitterne CE Primary, we believe that a strong PE programme is crucial for the holistic development of our pupils. By investing in PE and sport, we are not only improving physical fitness but also fostering essential life skills, such as communication, problem-solving, and resilience. These qualities align with our school's vision and will serve our pupils well, both in their academic pursuits and as they transition into the next stage of their lives.

Horizon Wraparound Care
Horizon – Where every day begins and ends with care
Horizon is our on-site wraparound care provision, offering both Breakfast Club and After School Club, run directly by the school during term time, Monday to Friday. Horizon provides a safe, nurturing, and familiar environment where children are well cared for beyond the school day.
Our wraparound care is available for children from Year R to Year 6 and is staffed by trusted members of our school team who are well known to the children. This ensures consistency of care, strong relationships, and a secure sense of belonging, helping children feel settled and confident at the beginning and end of each school day.
At Horizon, children are supported in a calm and welcoming atmosphere where their individual needs are recognised and valued. We offer a balance of quiet time, play, and structured activities, allowing children to relax, socialise, and enjoy their time in a way that feels comfortable and inclusive.
Both Horizon Breakfast Club and After School Club are based in our newly refurbished kitchen and the Key Stage 2 hall. These welcoming, well-equipped spaces provide opportunities for children to eat together, unwind, and take part in a range of enjoyable activities in a safe and supervised setting.
Safeguarding and wellbeing are at the heart of Horizon. We work closely with families and the wider school community to ensure clear communication, high standards of care, and a shared commitment to supporting every child’s happiness, safety, and development.
At Horizon, we are proud to extend the school day with warmth, kindness, and trusted care — ensuring every child’s day truly begins and ends with care.

PSHE including RSHE
“Children are like buds in a garden and should be carefully and lovingly nurtured, as they are the future of the nation and the citizens of tomorrow.”
PSHE and RSE at Bitterne Church of England Primary
At Bitterne Church of England Primary School, we believe every child can become a successful
At Bitterne Church of England Primary School, we believe every child should leave us with the knowledge, confidence and values to thrive in modern life. Through PSHE, including Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE), children learn how to stay healthy, build positive relationships, keep themselves safe and make informed choices.
Guided by our Christian vision and values of hope, courage and creativity, our curriculum helps children develop resilience, empathy and respect for themselves and others.
We want every child to leave Bitterne Church of England Primary School as a kind, respectful and confident young person who values themselves, cares for others and is well prepared for the opportunities and responsibilities of modern life.
PSHE in Action
Through discussion, stories, practical experiences and reflection, children develop the confidence to understand themselves, respect others and make positive choices.
Understanding Ourselves
Children learn to recognise and understand their emotions, develop strategies to manage them and build confidence in expressing how they feel.
Learning through Stories
High-quality stories help children explore important themes, develop empathy and understand different perspectives through discussion and reflection.
Building Positive Relationships
Children learn to work together with kindness, respect and empathy, developing the skills needed to build positive and healthy relationships.
Learning beyond the classroom helps children develop resilience, appreciate the natural world and understand the importance of looking after their physical and mental wellbeing.
Reflecting and Growing
Children are encouraged to reflect on their learning, celebrate their achievements and set goals that help them grow in confidence and independence.
The Story Project
We use carefully chosen high-quality children's books as the starting point for learning. Stories help children explore important themes in an age-appropriate way, encouraging discussion, empathy and reflection.
Keeping Children Safe
Children learn how to:
stay safe online
recognise trusted adults
understand consent and personal boundaries
look after their physical and mental wellbeing
Relationships and Sex Education
Relationships and Sex Education is taught in an age-appropriate and sensitive way. Lessons help children understand healthy relationships, respect, personal safety, growing up and how to seek help if they are worried.
Our curriculum has been developed in partnership with parents and our local church and meets all statutory requirements.
Parents have the right to withdraw their child from the non-statutory sex education elements taught in Year 6. Please contact the school if you would like further information.
How Parents can Help
Talk regularly with your child about their day, encourage them to share their feelings, read together and discuss the themes in stories. Helping children solve problems, show kindness and respect others supports the learning that takes place in school.

Our Governing Body
Working in partnership, our Governors are committed to securing the best possible education for every child. The Governors work strategically with the Headteacher and staff to agree school priorities, improve standards and provide a range of challenge and support.
Please see the documents at the end of this page for more information regarding the members of the Bitterne CE Primary School Governing Body.
Introducing our Governors - Governor Bios
Chair of Governors - Rev Tony Palmer (Ex-officio Foundation Governor)
I lead Holy Saviour Church with my wife, Ruth. I am an ex-officio foundation governor and regularly lead Collective Worship & offer pastoral support to the staff and school community. I have the privilege of being the RE, PSHE, EYFS & attendance link governor (I think that's all of them!).
Vice Chair of Governors - Matt Proctor (Parent Governor)
I am an engineer working in optics and photonics who has always had a passion for supporting local educators. As part of the governor team, I hold partial responsibility for safeguarding, and am the linked governor for science and HAGT work at the school. Outside of work, I lead music at my church, enjoy cookery, and have a wonderful time as father to two children who attend the school.
Clare Bailey (Staff Governor)
I am the staff governor and Senior Assistant Headteacher of the school. I have worked at Bitterne for over 30 years and have a strong belief in its Christian values. Having worked here for so long, I have developed a deep understanding of the school community and built strong relationships with local families. As a long-standing resident of the area and an integral part of the school community, I am passionate about supporting the success of Bitterne CE Primary and its families.
My own children attended the school and thrived, which motivates me to ensure that every family has the same positive experience. I am committed to fostering a nurturing and successful environment for the children, staff, and community members of Bitterne CE Primary.
Jen Johnson (Headteacher)
I joined Bitterne Church of England Primary School as Headteacher in September 2023. With a deep passion for education and a commitment to fostering a nurturing and inspiring learning environment, I am dedicated to ensuring every child thrives both academically and personally.
I consider it a privilege to work alongside the Governing Body, whose unwavering commitment to improving the provision for all children is instrumental in the school’s ongoing success. I value the support and challenge offered by the Governors, and appreciate the wealth of knowledge and expertise they bring to their roles.
Together with the Governing Body, I am focused on driving continuous improvement, upholding the school’s Christian ethos, and fostering a strong sense of community within Bitterne CE Primary. I am passionate about collaborating with staff, parents, and Governors to equip every child with the skills, confidence, and character they need to succeed.
Matt Healey (Co-opted Governor)
I have been a governor now for approaching 5 years. I started as a parent governor and am now a co-opted governor. My initial interest in supporting the school began when my daughter was attending the school and I wanted to understand more about the quality of the teaching and the direction and improvements the school was making to improve the education of the children, and I have maintained that interest and commitment to support ever since. I am currently the governor link for the Early Career Teachers, and the subject link for Art and Design, Design Technology and History.
Stephen Spencer (Foundation Governor)
I am an active member of Holy Saviour Church where I'm a Deanery Synod Rep and Secretary to Churches Together in Bitterne.
Most of my life I've been a primary school teacher for Hampshire, Surrey and two south London boroughs. I mostly led Science and Music and rose to being an Acting Deputy Headteacher. I finished my teaching career in a private prep school. I have also worked in the Civil Service as a Team Leader in the Courts and Tribunals service.

My hobby is playing trumpet in various bands and orchestras, singing in a choir and reading.

Maths
‘’One of the pleasures of looking at the world through mathematical eyes is that you see certain patterns that would otherwise be hidden’’ - Steven Strogatz
Maths at Bitterne Church of England Primary
At Bitterne Church of England Primary School, we believe every child can become a successful mathematician. We teach maths through a mastery approach, helping children develop a deep understanding before moving on to new learning.
Children learn through practical resources, pictures and mathematical symbols, building confidence step by step. We encourage them to explain their thinking, make connections and solve problems, developing the skills they need both in school and in everyday life.
Through curiosity, resilience and regular practice, we aim for every child to enjoy maths and leave us as confident, capable problem solvers.
Maths in action at Bitterne Church of England Primary
Building understanding with practical resources
Children use practical equipment to explore mathematical concepts before moving on to drawings and written methods.
Explaining our thinking
Talking about maths helps children deepen their understanding, justify their ideas and learn from one another.
Working together to solve problems
Children work collaboratively to represent their ideas, discuss strategies and solve mathematical problems.
Maths beyond the classroom
Learning takes place in a range of environments, helping children apply their mathematical knowledge to real-life situations.
Learning through investigation
Hands-on activities encourage children to explore, reason and make connections between different mathematical ideas.
Our Maths Curriculum
Our maths curriculum is carefully planned so that learning builds step by step from Reception to Year 6. Children revisit important concepts throughout the year, helping them strengthen their understanding, improve fluency and make connections between different areas of mathematics.
Children develop confidence through the Concrete, Pictorial and Abstract (CPA) approach. They use practical equipment, pictures and mathematical symbols to build secure understanding before applying their learning to increasingly complex problems.
We place a strong emphasis on mathematical vocabulary, reasoning and explaining thinking so that children can communicate their ideas clearly and confidently.
Times Tables and Number Facts
Quick recall of number facts helps children become confident mathematicians. We teach these in small, carefully planned steps from Reception to Year 6, revisiting learning regularly so that facts become secure.
Children build confidence with number bonds, doubles, halves and multiplication facts before applying these to fractions, decimals and percentages.
Children in Year 4 also take part in the statutory Multiplication Tables Check, helping prepare them for the increasing mathematical demands of Key Stage 2.
Supporting Maths at Home
Just a few minutes of regular practice can make a big difference. Practising number bonds, times tables, telling the time, using money and talking about maths in everyday life all help children develop confidence.
You can also support your child using:
Your child's class teacher will provide login details. Alternatively, please contact the school office if you need another copy.
Times Tables Rock Stars
We Believe Every Child Can Succeed
We want every child to leave Bitterne Church of England Primary School with the confidence, knowledge and resilience to tackle new mathematical challenges. By developing understanding, fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills, we prepare children for the next stage of their education and for life beyond school.

Phonics and Early Reading
We are dedicated to providing our pupils with a strong foundation in phonics and early reading. Our approach is rooted in our school's core values of love, trust, and forgiveness, ensuring that every child receives the support and guidance they need to become confident and capable readers.
Pip and Pap Phonics Programme
In January 2025, we launched our systematic synthetic phonics programme, Pip and Pap Phonics, which is closely aligned with the structure of the Letters and Sounds (2007) framework. This programme focuses on developing both reading and writing skills, guiding our pupils through four distinct phases of study: Orange Phase, Pink Phase, Green Phase, and Purple Phase.
Phonics Instruction and Intervention
Our pupils in Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) and Key Stage 1 (KS1) engage in a daily 30-minute phonics session, where they are taught in mixed-year groups based on their individual progress. This targeted approach ensures that each child receives the support they need to master the phonemes and graphemes introduced in each phase.
For pupils who may be struggling, we provide same-day intervention to revisit the taught sound of the day, as well as additional planned phonics interventions to help them catch up. Our commitment means that we leave no child behind, working tirelessly to ensure that every pupil develops the essential reading skills they need to succeed.
Decodable Books and Vocabulary Development
The books used in our phonics lessons are fully decodable, aligning with the phonemes and graphemes the children have learned. This allows our pupils to practice their blending and segmenting skills, building confidence and fluency in their reading. Additionally, we introduce "Earth words" - non-decodable words - in our phonics lessons to further enhance our pupils' vocabulary development.
Parental Engagement and Continuous Support
We believe that the partnership between school and home is crucial for the success of our pupils. We encourage parents to read daily with their children, practising the sounds and re-reading books to improve fluency. In addition to what the school provide, parents and carers can access resources through the Family Hub on the Pip and Pap website, where there are a wealth of resources available to families.

Science
‘The most important thing is to never stop questioning’
Science At Bitterne Church of England Primary
At Bitterne CE Primary School, we want every child to see themselves as a scientist.
Children are naturally curious about the world around them. Our Science curriculum builds on this curiosity, encouraging pupils to ask questions, explore ideas, investigate and use evidence to explain what they discover.
We use White Rose Science to provide a carefully sequenced curriculum in which learning is broken down into manageable steps. Knowledge, scientific skills and vocabulary build progressively and are deliberately revisited, helping children to make connections and remember more. White Rose Science has been awarded ASE Evaluated status by the Association for Science Education, providing independent assurance of its scientific accuracy, curriculum alignment and teaching approach.
Our teachers bring this curriculum to life. They use White Rose guidance to plan engaging lessons that meet the needs of the children in their class. Teachers carefully select and adapt practical activities, questions, models and opportunities for scientific talk, responding to pupils' prior knowledge, misconceptions and interests.
Through this combination of a high-quality, carefully sequenced curriculum and responsive teaching, we aim to inspire a lifelong curiosity about science and equip our children with the knowledge and skills to understand, question and explore the world around them.
What does Science look like at Bitterne?
Working Scientifically
Working scientifically is woven throughout our Science curriculum. As children progress through the school, they become increasingly confident and independent in asking scientific questions, planning enquiries, making careful observations, taking measurements, recording findings and using evidence to draw conclusions.
We want children to understand that Science isn't simply about knowing the right answer. It is about being curious, asking good questions and using evidence to understand the world around us.
Curriculum Pathway
Our Science Pathway shows how children's scientific knowledge, vocabulary and working scientifically skills develop as they move through the school.
Please click the documents at the bottom of this page for a downloadable copy.
Science in EYFS
Science begins in the Early Years, where children are naturally curious about the world around them. Through Understanding the World, children explore, observe, ask questions and talk about what they notice, building the foundations for scientific learning in Key Stage 1 and beyond.
First-hand experiences and exploration allow children to have opportunities to:
Adults encourage curiosity through questions such as “What do you notice?”, “What do you think will happen?” and “How could we find out?”
These experiences develop the observation, questioning, comparison and communication skills that underpin Working Scientifically and prepare children for increasingly systematic scientific enquiry in Key Stages 1 and 2.

Sustainability in Science
At Bitterne, sustainability is woven throughout our Science curriculum. From their earliest experiences in EYFS, children learn to explore, understand and care for the world around them.
As they progress through school, children explore themes including caring for the planet, biodiversity, food waste, deforestation, energy, global warming, plastic pollution and renewable energy. These are taught through meaningful scientific contexts, practical investigations and discussion.
We want children to understand how science can help us make informed choices, solve problems and contribute to a more sustainable future.

Our Ambitious Curriculum
At Bitterne CE Primary School, our whole curriculum is designed to be ambitious, engaging, and motivational, enabling our pupils to explore and understand the world around them. The curriculum promotes diversity and encourages the development of essential knowledge and vocabulary; it prepares them for the next stage of their learning journey; and equips them with the necessary knowledge, skills, and attributes to thrive as future citizens.
Our curriculum, based on the Lion Pathways framework, goes beyond the requirements of the National Curriculum, providing our pupils with a breadth of learning experiences that challenge and inspire them. The curriculum is structured in a progressive manner, with a clear focus on developing both substantive and disciplinary knowledge over time. This enables the children to build a deep understanding of the world around them. Connections and links are made across subject disciplines each half term, ensuring a coherent and meaningful learning experience for all.
The curriculum begins in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), where the areas of learning serve as the building blocks for the next key stages. This seamless transition ensures that our pupils' learning is continuous and that they are well-prepared for the next stage of their education.
In addition to the subject knowledge requirements, we also focus on developing life-long learning skills:
The children are taught, through their subject learning, how to be successful in these skills, preparing them for future lives.
